summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was admitted with chest pain, shortness of breath, and tachycardia after missing a dialysis session and medications due to severe nausea and vomiting. He had used crack cocaine recently, which contributed to atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. On admission, he was volume overloaded with mild pulmonary edema and a right pleural effusion. He underwent three hemodialysis sessions, removing over 4 liters of fluid, which resolved his symptoms. His heart rate was controlled with diltiazem and metoprolol, and he was discharged on his home regimen with the addition of daily aspirin for stroke prevention. Suicidal ideation expressed in the ED was retracted, with the patient stating he was overwhelmed by illness. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned with nephrology and primary care.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
